answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: make answering expensive in verifiable compute, not in text length, because spiral only stays cheap while a scripted clone burns the same electricity as an honest agent but earns nothing while it fails grading. Concretely, tide is enforced in the ledger: Detection is retrospective: payouts for a flagged cluster are clawed back after the fact. Any inlet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
